title: Conventional versus fascial rowing: Effects on myofascial lumbar stiffness
summary:
Rowing exercise is widely used to strengthen the back extensor muscles. In addition to muscular effects, it has been suggested that specific movement variations may also influence the thoracolumbar fascia and other myofascial tissues.
In this study, 30 healthy adults are randomly assigned to one of two training groups. One group performs ten minutes of conventional rowing exercise on a WaterRower rowing machine. The second group performs a modified fascial-focused rowing technique involving alternating lateral trunk and leg positions to increase loading outside the sagittal plane.
Measurements are performed immediately before and after the intervention. These include lumbar spine flexibility, tissue stiffness of the lower back region, and skin mobility.
The aim of the study is to investigate whether a fascial-focused rowing technique induces different immediate changes in mechanical properties of the lumbar myofascial tissues compared with conventional rowing.
conditions: Physiological characteristics of lumbar myofascial tissues in healthy adults.

interventions.name:
Conventional rowing: 
10 minute of rowing in conventional style on a Waterrower rowing machine.
Execution of rowing motion as in the instruction videos of the manufacturer.

Fascial-focused rowing:
10 minutes of exercise on a WaterRower Club rowing machine involving alternating lateral displacement of foot placement and trunk flexion, designed to increase multidirectional mechanical loading of the thoracolumbar fascia. Single application of 10 minutes duration.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy adults
* No acute or chronic low back pain
* No known spinal disorders
* Ability to safely perform a 10-minute rowing exercise session
* Written informed consent obtained prior to participation
* Absence of any exclusion criteria
Exclusion criteria:
* Acute or chronic low back pain
* Known spinal disorders
* Spinal surgery within the previous 12 months
* Neurological disorders
* Pregnancy
* Acute illness at the time of participation
* Current injuries or other physical impairments that could interfere with the safe performance of the rowing intervention
* Contraindications to physical exercise
